workflow_architecture_correction.description: Macro-stage W02 was erroneously decomposed into a sequential chain of 12 subruns (W2-01 through W2-12). This decomposition was terminated. Completed subruns W2-01 through W2-09 are preserved as valid historical evidence-generation runs. Proposed subruns W2-10, W2-11, and W2-12 are designated SUPERSEDED_BY_W02_CLOSEOUT and NOT executed.

scientific_gate_details.interpretation: BLOCKED indicates the candidate is not authorized to claim novelty survival because critical scientific threats remain unresolved. It does NOT signify a failed thesis or non-novelty.

key_findings: H0b sufficiency remains untested under locked calibration
Global M-kappa data are non-identifying for micro-mechanisms
Chamber pressure p is a boundary condition, not an identified contact force f_n
Locked calibration rule remains a protocol requirement, not demonstrated empirical evidence
Slip / transformation coexistence remains an unproven feasibility hypothesis
Citation closure is protocol closure, not universal novelty proof
Existing contact/cable incremental formulations remain plausible competitors
Thermal, frictional, training, and geometry confounding remain active

citation_protocol_closure.caveat: Citation protocol closure satisfies stopping conditions under the protocol; it does NOT prove universal absence of prior art in the broader literature.

reconciled_hypotheses.logical_rule: H0a false does NOT imply H1 true

current_mp1_candidate.label: CURRENT_MP1_CANDIDATE
current_mp1_candidate.formulation: Across a declared, experimentally accessible range of positive confinement pressure, curvature, and temperature where both inter-wire slip and stress-induced Martensitic transformation coexist, does an established transformation-aware NiTi constitutive and Coulomb-contact model (H0b) under locked parameter calibration adequately predict the pressure-dependent moment-curvature response, tangent bending stiffness, hysteresis loops, and local slip/transformation observables of a superelastic NiTi wire bundle, or does model failure under held-out conditions demonstrate the necessity of a novel constitutive-contact coupling law (H1)?
what_is_excluded: Device-level novelty (closed by Bai 2022, Liu 2021, Takashima 2022-2026, Wang 2024)
Generic pressure-controlled stiffness novelty (demoted to boundary condition p(t))
